title: Password Rotation: Tips + How to Do It Right
content_md: Good password habits now depend more on having a strong, unique password for each account. Changing it every 90 days or so made sense when people had fewer accounts to manage. Today, rotating passwords too often can lead to weak or repeated passwords that are easier to guess. And the numbers back it up, with our password statistics showing that 1 in 4 people report having at least one account compromised because of a weak one. The same rules apply to your personal accounts and home devices. A strong password can still leak in a data breach , so you need a plan for what happens next. We’ll discuss a few password rotation best practices that can help protect your accounts even after a password gets out. What Is Password Rotation? Password rotation means replacing a password or other login credential with a new one. You might do this on a set schedule, such as every few months, or after a security event, such as a password leak. The concept of password rotation can apply to more than the password you use to log in to your email or social media.
